clue.text: Those emerging victorious in foreign fields

explanation.surface: Soldiers come home triumphant from battles abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champs' is the French word for fields, hence 'foreign fields'.
explanation.definitionFit: Winners are informally champs, short for champions; in French the same word means meadows or fields.

clue.text: Frame nationalist charged with treason

explanation.surface: An Irish nationalist is framed and charged with treason.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Casement, the Irish nationalist, was hanged for treason in 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: A window frame hinged at the side is a casement; Roger Casement was the Irish patriot tried for treason.

clue.text: A superior who offers encouragement?

parts.note: a superior person or thing is better

explanation.surface: A boss who cheers on the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: one who abets offers encouragement, and the wordplay is A plus a word for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or assist, so one who abets is a supporter or encourager.

clue.text: Pram sheet made fancy with ribbon

indicators.note: made into something fancy means the letters are reworked into an ornate new order

explanation.surface: A pram's bedding is decorated with a ribbon trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a stiff corded ribbon used for hatbands and waistbands.

clue.text: Fellow taken in by short account rebuffed story-teller

indicators.note: taken in by tells us the fellow goes inside the other piece
rebuffed, pushed back, tells us the shortened account is read backwards
short means the last letter of the account word is dropped

parts.note: a record is an account of events
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man is drawn into a brief account and then rejected by a story-teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter, 'rebuffed' turns the remainder round to ROCER, and 'taken in by' puts the fellow inside; 'story-teller' means a spinner of fanciful tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A romancer invents fanciful tales, so is a teller of stories.

clue.text: Where there may be a different set of digits, however

definitions.text: Where there may be a different set of digits

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where another set of fingers might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is read literally: your other hand has another set of fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the opposite hand carries different fingers; as an idiom the phrase introduces a contrasting point, like 'but'.

clue.text: Sort of movement that draws male into island uprising

indicators.note: into tells us the male letter goes inside the island word
uprising, in a down clue, means the island is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A political movement draws a man into an island revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns ELBA into ABLE; M goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amble is a leisurely walking pace, a kind of movement, especially of a horse.

clue.text: Unceremonious dismissal by a novice in set

parts.note: a conge is an abrupt dismissal or curt leave-taking
L is the learner, a novice, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Someone is sacked without ceremony by a beginner on a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to set or thicken from liquid into solid, as jelly or fat does.

clue.text: Liking a smack

explanation.surface: A taste for being slapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a fondness or enjoyment, and also a flavour or trace, as a smack of garlic.

clue.text: Misses out in France

parts.note: the reading is plural young unmarried women, as addressed in French, not someone missing out

explanation.definitionFit: The French plural of mademoiselle, the title for unmarried women, corresponds to English Misses.

clue.text: You want fragrant lamb? Mint could be the answer

parts.note: sweet can mean pleasant-smelling, fragrant
lamb is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: A diner asks for scented lamb and is told mint sauce is the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the sauce for lamb; it is a mint sweet, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is a sugary confection, of which a mint is one example.

clue.text: Lacking that certain something to outlaw gangster

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Banning a mobster seems to lack any flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trite and unoriginal lacks distinction or spark.

clue.text: Drove and rode recklessly after vehicle test

indicators.note: after means the reckless ride follows the vehicle test in the answer

parts.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles

indicators.note: recklessly means the letters of the word rode are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone drove dangerously right after passing a car inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: To have motored is to have travelled by car, i.e. driven.

clue.text: Sides in English League initially level before introduction of substitute

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of English and League

parts.note: level means even, as in a level score
S is a common abbreviation for substitute on team sheets

explanation.surface: Football teams in an English league start level before a sub comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before introduction of' simply places S after EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket teams of eleven players are called elevens.

clue.text: Second Earl of Guildford may make declaration

explanation.surface: An aristocrat might issue a public statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North, Prime Minister in 1770-82, became second Earl of Guildford; in bridge the player seated North may declare the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick, Lord North, succeeded as second Earl of Guildford; at bridge the compass seat can become declarer.

clue.text: Warlike people potentially tameable

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A fierce nation that might yet be tamed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ndebele of Zimbabwe, a warrior nation historically known by this name, were renowned fighters.

clue.text: American port and British beer circulating round Indonesian island

indicators.note: circulating round means the British beer letters wrap around the island

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
Timor is an island in the Indonesian archipelago

explanation.surface: British beer is shipped around an Asian island before reaching an American harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore in Maryland is a major seaport city of the US.

clue.text: Keep something in the larder?

explanation.surface: Store a pot of jam in the pantry.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something safe is to conserve it, and jam or fruit conserve stored in a pantry is the same word.

clue.text: Sort of poisoning a pimento can produce

indicators.note: can produce suggests the letters of a pimento may be worked into something new

explanation.surface: A canned pepper might give you food poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a tin of pimentos; it is part of the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are compounds from decaying protein once blamed for food poisoning, hence the old name for it.

clue.text: Land with water and more water? Not Western Australia

indicators.note: Not tells us the Australian state's letters are removed

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for the state of Western Australia
rain is more water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Ground that is wet and then rained on, though not in Western Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: WATER plus RAIN makes WATERRAIN; 'Not' removes WA.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of ground or landscape.

clue.text: Drink from Germany introduced by the French

indicators.note: introduced by means the French article comes first, before the country

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A German beer brought in by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: A legend is spurious, it's gathered

indicators.note: is spurious says the letters given are false in arrangement and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone concludes that a myth is fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' looks like 'inferred'; here it means collected, as harvest leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to collect bit by bit, so the past form means collected.

clue.text: Instruments providing form of jazz aboard

annotationWithheld.why: Instruments providing form of jazz aboard (6): STRADS is TRAD inside SS, but 'aboard' alone must give both the SS and the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Instruments providing form of jazz aboard

clue.text: Anguish from wrong remedy suppressing cold

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: suppressing means the cold letter is kept down, taken out of the remedy

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Distress caused by the wrong treatment for a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' removes C from CURE, leaving URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Torture is extreme pain or mental agony.

clue.text: Working for international organisation upset revolutionary

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, means the revolutionary word is turned upside down

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary, a communist

explanation.surface: A staffer at a world body is upset by a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To work beneath someone is to serve as their subordinate.

clue.text: Rudolf, full of anger, won't succeed as a man

indicators.note: full of means the Nazi's name contains the anger word

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy
ire means anger

explanation.surface: An angry Nazi deputy fails to make it as a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy; the definition means she will inherit, but as a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female successor to an estate inherits, but not in a male role.

clue.text: Ace section of hospital gets the prize

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A top-rated hospital department wins an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition.

clue.text: One with estate can show you way round county, right

indicators.note: round means the way word goes around the county

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A squire offers to show you the right route around his county.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner of land holds an estate.

clue.text: Garment beginning to squeeze? Then strip!

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of squeeze

parts.note: to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A tight item of clothing that must be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundress is a light sleeveless summer frock, an item of clothing.

clue.text: 'Busy' type nabbing bad lad?

indicators.note: nabbing means the busy insect grabs and holds the jumbled boy inside it

parts.note: a bee is the proverbial busy creature

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of lad are garbled

explanation.surface: A policeman grabs a young troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles the boy and 'nabbing' sets him inside the insect; the whole clue pictures the officious Victorian parish constable collaring a young rascal, and 'Busy' is also British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The old parish constable in Victorian England kept order, catching miscreants like Oliver Twist.
